abstract_ssh: Fix wait_up() when timeout is not specified If timeout is not specified, the local variable 'end_time' would be referenced before assignment, causing runtime error. To fix this, we should have a default timeout since it doesn't make sense to wait forever in practical use cases. Besides, since the timeout to wait for DUT up is implemented by the while loop, not by the args passed to is_up(), we should tweak 'timeout' and 'connect_timeout' args passed to is_up() to make wait_up() more efficient. glibc : backport optimizations from 2.28 This backports a patch that optimizes strcmp/wcscmp, and strncmp/wcsncmp with AVX2 on x86_64 platforms. Current glibc shows 788 avx2 instructions, with this patch, avx2 instructions has been increased to 1076: commit 1457016337072d1b6739f571846b619596990cb7 Author: Leonardo Sandoval <leonardo.sandoval.gonzalez@linux.intel.com> Date: Thu May 3 11:09:30 2018 -0500 x86-64: Optimize strcmp/wcscmp and strncmp/wcsncmp with AVX2 Optimize x86-64 strcmp/wcscmp and strncmp/wcsncmp with AVX2. It uses vector comparison as much as possible. Peak performance observed on a SkyLake machine: 9x, 3x, 2.5x and 5.5x for strcmp, strncmp, wcscmp and wcsncmp, respectively. The larger the comparison length, the more benefit using avx2 functions, except on the strcmp, where peak is observed at length == 32 bytes. Select AVX2 strcmp/wcscmp on AVX2 machines where vzeroupper is preferred and AVX unaligned load is fast. NB: It uses TZCNT instead of BSF since TZCNT produces the same result as BSF for non-zero input. TZCNT is faster than BSF and is executed as BSF if machine doesn't support TZCNT. Credits to Vaibhav Shankar for identifying these changes. BUG=None TEST=Cherrypick this patch and bootstrap the sdk. Then build for any x86 platform.
